## Natural history notes

A medium-sized forester moth characterized by its dark bluish-black wings marked with bold white or pale yellow spots and a sturdy, wasp-like body. In Florida, it is found in pine flatwoods, scrub, dry prairies, forest edges, roadsides, and other sunny open habitats where suitable host plants and nectar sources occur. Adults are active during the day and often visit flowers, while the caterpillars feed on native vines in the grape family, helping link open woodland plant communities with pollinating and herbivorous insects.
